newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares rise, eye Wall Street for clues.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares rise, eye Wall Street for clues.

text.p: Polish shares rebounded after a three-session fall on Tuesday, following Monday's Wall Street gains, and analysts said investors were likely to keep watching the U.S. market before making their investment decisions.
The main market's WIG index rose 1.2 percent, to 16,038.5, and turnover rose 8.4 percent to 174.4 million zlotys ($58 million) on all three markets as 53 issues rose, 15 fell and 25 were flat.
"Our market keeps imitating Dow Jones as our investors act on expectations of large foreign investor decisions," said Cezary Markiewicz, an analyst at Bank Gdanski brokerage.

Analysts said March 0.8 percent month-on-month inflation, realeased on Tuesday, was lower than expected, but said it was likely to have an effect on the market only in the longer-term seeing a rate-cut no sooner than in the second half of 1997.

Some analysts said the Warsaw bourse was unlikely to experience strong gains at least in the next few weeks due to current and forthcoming large and attractive primary market offers and expected a horizontal trend or falls.

The paper firm Celuloza Swiecie SA's primary market offer of at least 112.5 million zlotys ($37.5 million) started on Tuesday and the metals trader Impexmetal SA will offer at least 222-million-zloty ($74 million) shares next week.

Some analysts also said that some investors were likely to postpone major investment decison until after Polish parliamentary elections due in autumn and expected more significant growth only in the end of the year.

Traders said the debt-ridden construction company Espebepe SA surged 10 percent but did not trade after price fixing due to excess demand on speculation that the firm might still win a debt write-off deal.
Continuous trade turnover amounted to 13.5 million zlotys ($4.5 million) with the WIG 20 index closing flat at 1,585.7.
